These pages are working prototypes toward a small, readable course textbook rather than a stack of slides. The current pass establishes the equations and main reasoning. Many pages still need tighter writing, figures, live questions, and tested notebooks.

## Companion books and formats

Many topics use the formats of two companion books alongside these notes.

- Eric Sullivan's *Numerical Methods: An Inquiry-Based Approach with Python* supplies question-driven investigations. Use the [online book](https://numericalmethodssullivan.github.io/index.html) and its [GitHub source](https://github.com/NumericalMethodsSullivan/NumericalMethodsSullivan.github.io/tree/master) when a page assigns a Sullivan-style activity.
- Jaan Kiusalaas's *Numerical Methods in Engineering with Python 3* supplies concise equation → algorithm → Python examples. The book is available from [Cambridge University Press](https://doi.org/10.1017/CBO9781139523899) and through the University library.

These books are companions, not material to memorize cover to cover. Read the section named by the lecture or seminar.
